subject: ACME — Pricing estimate & token usage follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: ACME discovery recap & next steps (token volumes + budget)

Alex — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through ACME's planned rollout. Quick recap and the asks I promised below.

Key points from our call:
- Primary use case: in-product generative assistant for sales reps (summary + suggestion).
- Expected active users: 1,200 seat licenses by end of Q4.
- Per-rep monthly usage estimate: 40 sessions, avg 250 tokens/session (prompt + response) => ~10k tokens/user/month.
- Projected initial 1M-token throughput bucket: targeting 100M tokens/month for pilot with growth to 500M tokens/month in 12 months.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm target monthly token volume range (pilot vs steady-state)? You mentioned a likely pilot of 100-150M/month.
2) What's the procurement timeline and any internal budget guardrails (target $/1M tokens)?
3) I'll send a preliminary cost model and invoice estimate (spreadsheet) for review — will include options: hosted API, reserved dedicated pool, and recommended quantization for cost savings.

I've attached an initial pricing model template to show unit economics. If you can confirm the expected token distribution (short vs long responses) I can tighten the numbers.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up with procurement if needed.

—Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: acme_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2026-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME discovery recap & next steps (token volumes + budget)

Sean — thanks for the recap and for the fast turnaround. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Pilot expected: 100M-150M tokens/month for the first 3 months. Steady-state target after full rollout: ~400-500M tokens/month.
- Token mix: ~70% short responses (<=200 tokens), 30% longer summaries (~600 tokens) — this will matter for per-token execution time.
- Budget: We have a target of $600–$900 per 1M tokens for the pilot procurement line-item; open to tradeoffs if reserved capacity or committed pricing reduces unit costs.
- Procurement timeline: procurement evaluation starting 6/15, legal review late June. Decision expected by mid-July.

I attached our internal usage worksheet (redacted) to help calibrate. Would be great to see a hosted vs dedicated cost comparison with assumed quantization savings.

Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product | ACME Corp
alex.morgan@acme.ai

Attachments: acme_internal_usage_redacted.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2026-06-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME discovery recap & next steps (token volumes + budget)

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarity. I updated the model with your token mix and budget range. Two scenarios below and attached a more detailed workbook (redwood_cost_calc.csv + PDF summary).

Scenario A — Hosted (no commit):
- Pilot (100M/month): list price baseline ~ $1,200 per 1M tokens -> est monthly cost: $120k (before volume discounts).
- With standard volume tiering and short-response skew, effective blended rate ~ $900–$1,000 per 1M tokens.

Scenario B — Dedicated (3-12 month reserved capacity):
- Pilot committed pricing target: $600–$800 per 1M tokens (matches your target range) depending on commit level and quantization (int8/int4) we can reach lower unit costs.
- For 150M/month (pilot ceiling): estimated monthly invoice ~ $90k–$120k with reserved discounts and autoscale buffer.

Notes on assumptions in the model:
- We modeled prompt/response distribution per your mix and included KV/prefix caching assumptions (saves ~10-15% tokens on repeated prompts).
- Quantization: int8 yields ~20-30% cheaper GPU-hours vs fp16 on our runtime; int4 path gives higher token throughput but requires model compatibility testing.
- Ops overhead & SLA add-ons not included in base numbers — will add line items if you want SLA-backed Dedicated pricing.

I've attached: redwood_cost_calc.csv (detailed cost calc), 20260603-acme-estimate.pdf (one-page summary). Let me know if you want me to split out storage/egress, or present a per-seat monthly view for your finance team.

If this looks good, can we schedule a 30-min pricing review next week with procurement + finance? I'm free Tue/Wed afternoons (PDT).

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_cost_calc.csv, 20260603-acme-estimate.pdf
